title: run.json
description: Summary of one run of the backend pipeline. Its presence marks a directory as a run directory.

language.description: Which backend produced the run, e.g. `java` or `dotnet`. The extension uses it only to pick the backend command for run-tests.

target.description: The procedure whose calls were recorded.

signature.description: Full signature in the language's own notation, e.g. `com.example.Divider.divide(int,int)`.

captured.description: The recorded arguments and fields, in display order. Snapshots in trace.json are keyed by `captureId`.

typeNames.description: Short display names for type names used anywhere in the run (values, `captured`, exception types), e.g. `System.Int32` → `int`, `com.example.Node` → `Node`. The UI shows the short name and the full name on hover; a type that isn't listed is shown as it is.

traceMode.description: How the backend recorded the trace, e.g. `naive` or `temporal`. Shown in the run summary only.

recorded.description: What the backend records for each call. A `false` flag means the matching field is omitted from every call in trace.json.

counts.description: Sizes of trace.json and tests.json, so a run can be summarized without reading them.

status.description: Result of the full run's own work: recording the calls and generating the tests. `ok` when both succeeded, `failed` otherwise; a failed run may still have some of the other files. Failures while executing tests (e.g. the tests don't compile) are reported in results.json only; run-tests never changes run.json.

error.description: Why recording or test generation failed, when `status` is `failed`. Shown in the Runs view.

kind.description: Whether the value is shown under Arguments or Fields.

name.description: Shown as the value's name. An argument whose real name the backend doesn't know is named `arg<position>`, counting from 0 (`arg0`, `arg1`, …). If two captured fields would have the same name (e.g. fields of different classes), the backend makes them distinct, e.g. `Other.count`.
